## Summary

CodeQL open alert on default branch: **HIGH** `js/bad-tag-filter` — Bad HTML filtering regexp.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Alert | [#109](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/109) |
| Rule | `js/bad-tag-filter` |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Location | `packages/core/src/spec-authority/spec-authority.test.ts` ~L601 |
| Message | This regular expression only parses --> and not --!> as a HTML comment end tag. |

## What to build

Rewrite or bound the flagged site so CodeQL `js/bad-tag-filter` clears for this alert (or document accepted risk with suppress + rationale if false positive after review). Prefer a real fix over suite-config changes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] CodeQL alert [#109](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/109) clears on master (auto-close or dismiss with reason after fix).
- [ ] Existing unit tests for the touched module still pass; add adversarial input coverage if useful.
- [ ] CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #109.

## Non-goals

- Changing CodeQL suite config as the primary fix.
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue (siblings tracked separately).

## In plain English

CodeQL alert #109 flags a HIGH js/bad-tag-filter hit on a unit-test assertion that counts literal --> closers in a generated SPECIFICATION.md source banner. The test is proving path-encoding (--> becomes --%3E) so a malicious filename cannot break the HTML comment; it is not an HTML sanitizer. Prefer-A rewrites that assertion so it no longer looks like an incomplete HTML-comment filter, keeps the encoding invariants, and refuses suite-config or suppress as the primary fix.

## Proposed Bound remedy (draft — critics refute before bind)

relieves: P1
- In packages/core/src/spec-authority/spec-authority.test.ts (keeps unsafe explicit spec filename bytes), replace expect(sourceLine?.match(/-->/g)).toHaveLength(1) with a non-HTML-filter assertion that still proves exactly one literal three-character --> closer remains in the banner (for example indexOf/lastIndexOf equality, or split("-->").length === 2). Keep the existing --%3E / %0D%0A / %5C contains checks.
relieves: P1
- Prefer string/index counting over expanding to a complete HTML-comment-end regex that also matches --!> unless the critic shows that complete-pattern regex is required for CodeQL clearance AND preserves the encoding invariant. Do not introduce a production HTML sanitizer.
relieves: P1
- Keep unit tests green for the touched module; add a brief adversarial note or assertion only if useful that encoded path bytes do not introduce a second comment-closer form.
relieves: P1
- CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #109.

## Reject

- Changing .github/codeql/codeql-config.yml (or paths-ignore / query suite) as the primary fix.
- Dismissing alert #109 as false-positive without rewriting the flagged site.
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts.
- Rewriting production renderSpec / encoding logic beyond what the assertion rewrite requires.

- packages/core/src/spec-authority/spec-authority.test.ts
- CHANGELOG.md

Round 1, fresh critic; open critique; N=1. Reviewed issue body and comments through 6256527851, with source pinned to 8341f369ccc55fa907abd5e575bb29556e467e9f.

Prefer-A is sufficient as the design direction for P1. Removing the incomplete regexp from this test assertion while retaining the encoding and resolver checks is a bounded remedy. No production sanitizer, suite change, dismissal, or unrelated alert work is justified by this site. This is design endorsement, not measured CodeQL clearance or a pain-audit clearance.

### F1 — sharpens-framing — Make the replacement reject zero closers
Evidence: [draft](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/5741#issuecomment-6256521341) offers indexOf/lastIndexOf equality; [pinned test L593-L603](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/8341f369ccc55fa907abd5e575bb29556e467e9f/packages/core/src/spec-authority/spec-authority.test.ts#L593) currently requires exactly one match. A read-only Node truth-table check gives equality=true for both zero and one closer, because the absent case compares -1 with -1. The existing contains checks do not themselves require a literal closing delimiter.
Failure mode: a missing banner closer can pass that proposed replacement and weaken the original invariant.
Consequence: the design can bind, but specify split("-->").length === 2 on a defined source line, or require indexOf("-->") >= 0 in addition to first/last equality. Keep the three encoded-byte checks and both resolver checks.

### F2 — sharpens-framing — Preserve the actual verification endpoint
Evidence: the pinned L566 skips this test on win32; L588 supplies a filename containing CR/LF, -->, and backslash; L601 matches only -->. The issue body requires alert #109 to clear on master. The draft's remedy explicitly requires green module tests but does not restate the post-fix CodeQL endpoint.
Failure mode: a Windows green suite can skip the changed assertion, and a syntactic rewrite alone cannot establish that the alert cleared.
Consequence: bind the existing issue acceptance explicitly: execute the touched test on a supported non-Windows runner and verify a CodeQL analysis containing the fix clears #109 on master. Keep dismissal and suite configuration out of the remedy. I used the prescribed pin-read verification path; no module tests or CodeQL analysis were executed in this critic run.

### F3 — footnote — Single-critic ceiling recording differs from the contract
Evidence: Stop 1 is 6256524779, while the envelope and deposit choose 6256527851 with N=1. The pinned contract's Envelope and ceiling section assigns the triage write-back as Round-1 ceiling when one exists; its post-deposit exception applies to N>=2. I honored the explicit envelope ceiling and did not re-ceiling. The additional input is dispatch metadata, so this does not change the product verdict. Record the discrepancy; do not claim this N=1 deposit follows the N>=2 exception.

### F4 — footnote — The CodeQL concern is narrower than a demonstrated production vulnerability
The source confirms that /-->/g excludes --!>, exactly as reported in the issue. Here it counts a literal delimiter in generated output; it does not sanitize input. Existing mechanisms already test encoded CR/LF, greater-than, and backslash bytes plus source resolution. A complete comment-end regexp is the strongest alternative if the intended assertion becomes HTML-parser safety, but that is a different invariant from counting the known banner delimiter. Evidence of unsafe production output would change this verdict; the flagged assertion alone does not establish it.

Recording handback: preserve each classified finding in the parent's disposition census. Any successor lean must state the accepted remedy and P1 disposition, and satisfy the contract's subsequent independent pain-audit and synthesis obligations; this Round-1 post with audit-targets: none does not discharge them. No implementation, ingest, label mutation, or PR work performed. EXIT.
